header.title: Dual-use rearmament spending spills over into advanced manufacturing and energy technology

s01_bottom_line.text: Increased spending on dual-use technologies is already providing a tailwind to other segments of the industrial economy such as advanced manufacturing and energy technology, with NATO's 5% target reserving up to 1.5% of GDP for defense-related investment in critical infrastructure, networks and the industrial base.
The article frames defense as becoming a pillar of industrial policy, with resilience spending reaching defense-adjacent companies and energy-tech offtakers.

A broadened security mandate (critical minerals, off-grid energy, infrastructure resilience) could widen the beneficiary set beyond pure-play defense, but the article names no listed beneficiaries and does not quantify the spillover.

The United States launched Project Vault, a large-scale effort to create a strategic critical mineral reserve
